question_text: In one hour, Isabelita can prepare 120 spring rolls, and Arturo can prepare 100 spring rolls.

subparts.stem:
How long will it take to prepare 600 spring rolls if:
Isabelita works by herself
subparts.solution: Isabelita can prepare $600$ spring rolls in $\frac{600}{120} = 5\text{ hours}$.

ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Dividing rate by total work instead of total work by rate.

subparts.stem:
How long will it take to prepare 600 spring rolls if:
Arturo works by himself
subparts.solution: Arturo can prepare $600$ spring rolls in $\frac{600}{100} = 6\text{ hours}$.

subparts.stem:
How long will it take to prepare 600 spring rolls if:
Isabelita and Arturo work together?

mark_breakdown.desc: Add rates: 1/5 + 1/6 = 11/30 of the job per hour
Take reciprocal to find total time: 30/11 hours

subparts.solution:
Isabelita can complete $\frac{120}{600} = \frac{1}{5}$ of the job each hour, and Arturo can complete $\frac{100}{600} = \frac{1}{6}$ of the job each hour.
So, working together they can complete $\frac{1}{5} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{11}{30}$ of the job each hour.
$\therefore$ it would take them $\frac{30}{11} \approx 2.73\text{ hours} \approx 2\text{ hours } 44\text{ minutes}$ to complete the job together.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Combined work rate is the sum of individual work rates.
step_by_step: Find combined rate: $120 + 100 = 220$ spring rolls per hour (or $\frac{1}{5} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{11}{30}$ of the job/hour).
Convert decimal hours to minutes: $\frac{8}{11} \times 60 \approx 43.6 \approx 44\text{ minutes}$.
Total time is approximately $2\text{ hours } 44\text{ minutes}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Averaging the two times $\frac{5+6}{2} = 5.5$ instead of adding rates.

subparts.stem: Discuss any assumptions you have made in a, and whether or not they are reasonable.
subparts.final_answer: $In a i and a ii: assumed constant work rate; in a iii: assumed they work together without hindering each other.$

mark_breakdown.desc: State and evaluate constant rate assumption for (a i) and (a ii)
State and evaluate independence/no hindrance assumption for (a iii)

subparts.solution:
In a i and a ii, we assume that Isabelita and Arturo can work at a constant rate over many hours. It is likely that they would slow down or need a rest, so this assumption may not be reasonable.
In a iii, we assume that Isabelita and Arturo can work without getting in each other's way. This assumption seems reasonable.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Assessing assumptions involves identifying the mathematical conditions imposed and discussing their realism in a practical context.
step_by_step: For individual work: constant productivity ignores fatigue and breaks.
For joint work: independent rates assume shared space does not decrease productivity.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Failing to explain whether the assumption is reasonable or not.
